paper.title: OGMP: Oracle Guided Multi-mode Policies for Agile and Versatile Robot Control
paper.source_version: arXiv v3, 2024-09-18; latest public arXiv version verified 2026-08-30. Official code evidence pinned to commit 085d293f4e8b494021e6bb93fb33b137b98ca6de.

decision_relevance.why_admitted: OGMP formalizes a receding-horizon state-reference oracle, mode decomposition, and a tunable permissible-state tube, then tests how oracle family, horizon, conditioning, and rho affect one-policy-per-task robot control.
not_evidence_for: automatic discovery, ranking, or composition of reference datasets
a reference-only intervention under an otherwise frozen MDP
vision-conditioned VIBE integration or a frozen foundation tracker
global policy coverage or global convergence
dynamic feasibility of every oracle reference

mechanisms.name: Receding-horizon oracle
mechanisms.description: Xi maps a current state x_t and task variant psi_T to a finite state-reference trajectory x^Xi[t,t+Delta t]. The conceptual contract assumes a reference exists for every input and remains within an unknown epsilon of an unknown optimal trajectory.

mechanisms.name: Oracle-bounded permissible state tube
mechanisms.description: Policy states are restricted to ||x^pi_t-x^Xi_t||_W<rho. The experiments realize the bound as early termination; the theory gives rho>=epsilon as a sufficient reachability condition, while practice grid-searches rho because epsilon is unknown.

mechanisms.name: Task-vital multi-modality
mechanisms.description: A user defines a finite set of spatially or temporally invariant trajectory segments and continuous mode parameters; repeated mode instances and transitions are intended to span an infinite-horizon task.

mechanisms.name: Linear, LQR, and preview-control oracles
mechanisms.description: The paper builds three oracle families over an approximate single-rigid-body LTI model. Preview control adds look-ahead demand; the oracle may use auxiliary moments and need not output physically realistic control.

mechanisms.name: Oracle-trajectory mode encoder
mechanisms.description: A single-hidden-layer 32-unit LSTM autoencoder compresses oracle reference horizons to a two-dimensional latent mode command z.

mechanisms.name: Recurrent mode-conditioned policy
mechanisms.description: A two-layer 128-node LSTM PPO policy observes robot proprioception, latent mode command z, a phase clock c, and optional task feedback h such as terrain scan.

mechanisms.name: Oracle-tracking surrogate reward
mechanisms.description: The per-step objective combines exponential base-position and base-orientation tracking, a control-magnitude term, and a non-toe-contact penalty. Its coefficients are shared across the two tasks, but its numerical target changes with the oracle.

mechanisms.name: Horizon-boundary online replanning
mechanisms.description: The released environment re-queries the oracle when the environment step count reaches a prediction-horizon boundary, then uses the resulting reference for conditioning, reward, and termination.

failure_modes.name: Unknown oracle quality
failure_modes.description: The proof sketch depends on epsilon, but both the optimum x* and epsilon are unknown; rho therefore requires empirical search.

failure_modes.name: Over-constrained exploration
failure_modes.description: If rho is too small, the optimal behavior can lie outside the permissible tube and training terminates before reaching it.

failure_modes.name: Under-constrained exploration
failure_modes.description: If rho is too large, additional local optima re-enter the search space; rho=0.8 and the unguided rho=10^10 baseline stagnated in the reported parkour analysis.

failure_modes.name: Short-horizon surrogate exploitation
failure_modes.description: At 7dt the parkour policy obtained high tracking objective while remaining stationary, showing that the surrogate can disagree with task progress.

failure_modes.name: Failure outside the oracle tube
failure_modes.description: Restricting reachable states sacrifices global policy coverage; the authors warn that states outside the rho-neighborhood can fail.

failure_modes.name: Manual task-vital mode specification
failure_modes.description: Mode identity and parameterization are user-defined; the paper does not test missing, redundant, or incorrect decompositions.

failure_modes.name: Latent conditioning did not improve parkour return
failure_modes.description: Adding z to terrain and clock observations did not improve the reported parkour objective; the authors retain z for analysis, reuse, and possible reactive commands.

failure_modes.name: Conceptual versus released closed-loop interface
failure_modes.description: The formal oracle accepts any current state, but released parkour uses selected live state components while released dive constructs x0 from task parameters or the previous reference endpoint.

failure_modes.name: Post-paper code cleanup drift
failure_modes.description: The official repository states that cleanup changed convergence and analysis results slightly, so current YAML is not sufficient proof of every reported checkpoint's exact configuration.

evaluation.name: HECTOR parkour and dive task suite
evaluation.description: One recurrent policy per task is evaluated on a 16-DoF biped: random block-gap parkour and omnidirectional diving. Parkour transfers to hardware; diving is reported in simulation.

evaluation.name: Parkour agility metrics
evaluation.description: Across 100 rollouts, the paper reports maximum heading acceleration, maximum heading speed, Froude number, and episode-length fraction for six observation variants.

evaluation.name: In-domain and out-of-domain terrain sweep
evaluation.description: The parkour policy is evaluated by undiscounted return over discretized jump/block and leap/gap dimensions inside and outside the training support.

evaluation.name: Oracle family by permissible-bound ablation
evaluation.description: Linear, LQR, and preview oracles are compared while varying rho. Preview control mattered for diving; parkour showed no significant oracle-family difference.

evaluation.name: Oracle-horizon ablation
evaluation.description: Seven-, fifteen-, and thirty-step horizons separate stationary, quasi-static, and agile block-to-block parkour behaviors and expose task-versus-tracking objective mismatch.

evaluation.name: Clock, terrain, and latent observation ablation
evaluation.description: Clock-bearing variants consistently outperform their counterparts; terrain feedback reduces myopia; latent conditioning adds no reported parkour return over terrain plus clock.

evidence.claim: The record lists Lokesh Krishna, Nikhil Sobanbabu, and Quan Nguyen; v3 dated 2024-09-18 is the latest public arXiv version and reports HECTOR parkour sim-to-real plus simulation diving.

Xi returns a finite-horizon reference from current state and task variant; the reference is assumed within unknown epsilon of an unknown optimum, while policy states are restricted to a rho-neighborhood and rho>=epsilon is sufficient for optimal-state reachability.
Task-vital modes are finite spatiotemporal segments with continuous parameters; sequences of these modes and transitions are proposed as a compact representation of infinite-horizon task variants.
The user-defined task decomposition is parkour pace {v}, jump {w,h}, leap {w,d}, and dive settle {}, flip {r,h}.

Linear, LQR, and preview oracles use an approximate SRB LTI system with a 13-dimensional state and 12-dimensional output/control; auxiliary aggregate moments and horizon-averaged orientations simplify the model.

The mode autoencoder has one 32-unit LSTM hidden layer and a 2-D latent; the policy observes proprioception, latent, clock, and optional task feedback; exact reward coefficients are given; the rho constraint is implemented as termination with sparse W; PPO uses a 2x128 LSTM.

Evaluation uses 100 rollouts, a 10 m/400-step parkour test and 150-step dive test, reports agility metrics across observation variants, in/out-of-domain mode-parameter behavior, and real parkour envelopes of 105% leg-length gaps, 20% robot-height blocks, and 0.6 m/s pacing.

Ablations vary observation components, oracle family, rho, and horizon. The paper reports no parkour return benefit from latent conditioning, oracle-dependent best rho, short-horizon task failure, parkour rho*=0.5 for preview, and the same local optimum for rho=0.8 and unguided rho=10^10.
The authors explicitly state that restricting reachable states forgoes a global policy and that states outside the rho-neighborhood may fail.
The official project page maps the tested horizons to 0.21, 0.45, and 0.9 seconds and labels their outcomes as failure, myopic block-ground-block motion, and optimal block-block transitions.

The pinned cleaned parkour configuration uses Kp=30, Kd=0.5, a 30-step preview oracle, selected translational state feedback, a 1 m terrain scan, a 0.3 x-reference termination threshold, 10 PD targets, and explicit block/gap supports.

The released parkour oracle query builds x0 from the current simulator state, replaces unselected components by nominal values, and passes selected state, forward terrain scan, and desired displacement [1,0].

The pinned cleaned dive configuration uses Kp=30, Kd=0.5, a 30-step preview oracle, a 0.1 z-reference termination threshold, 10 PD targets, and pitch/roll flip supports of height 1.0–1.75 and delta-theta -6.28–6.28.

The released dive oracle constructs x0 from sampled height for the flip and from the previous reference endpoint for settling, then passes x0, initial/final heights, and desired rotation; it does not read the live robot state in this function.
The released environment re-queries the oracle at prediction-horizon boundaries, applies the policy action, computes oracle-dependent rewards and termination, and also queries the oracle on reset.

The released trainer defaults specify 600M time steps, gamma 0.95, fixed action std 0.13, actor and critic learning rates 1e-4, KL threshold 0.02, gradient clip 0.05, batch 64, 8 epochs, 30 workers, and 50k samples per iteration.
